R-MED-001.name: PHI Identifier Detection
R-MED-001.description: All 18 HIPAA Safe Harbor PHI identifiers must be detected in ingested documents before processing proceeds.

R-MED-002.name: Encryption at Rest
R-MED-002.description: All ePHI must be encrypted with AES-256 (or equivalent) at rest on staging and SSD.

R-MED-003.name: Encryption in Transit
R-MED-003.description: All ePHI transmissions must use TLS 1.2 or higher.

R-MED-004.name: Minimum Necessary Standard
R-MED-004.description: Access to PHI must be limited to the minimum necessary for the intended purpose.

R-MED-005.name: Retention Period — Medical Records
R-MED-005.description: Medical document metadata and derived data must be retained for at least 6 years from creation or last effective date.

R-MED-006.name: Breach Notification — PHI
R-MED-006.description: Any breach of unsecured PHI affecting 500+ individuals must be reported to HHS within 60 days. Any breach affecting 500+ in a state requires AG and media notification. HITECH extends to 72-hour notification for large breaches.

R-MED-007.name: Access Audit Logging
R-MED-007.description: All access to ePHI must be logged with user identity, timestamp, and action performed.

R-MED-008.name: De-identification Standard
R-MED-008.description: Documents containing PHI must be de-identified per Safe Harbor or Expert Determination before any external sharing.
